 2027 Social Security COLA Is Official - Here's How Much 6 Types of Beneficiaries Will Get
 The latest increase will look different across households.
 By
 Adam Palasciano 
 ,
 Edited by
 Laura Hohenstein 
 Updated
 Nov. 2, 2026
 Fact checked 
 This article was subjected to a comprehensive fact-checking process. Our professional fact-checkers verify article information against primary sources, reputable publishers, and experts in the field.
 Add Us On Google
 Google Preferred Sources lets you customize your search results. By choosing to follow FinanceBuzz, you’re telling Google to prioritize content from a source you trust.
The Social Security Administration has officially announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027, giving millions of beneficiaries a larger monthly payment. The increase takes effect in January, helping offset rising prices for everyday essentials. If Social Security plays a major role in your retirement plan , knowing what that increase means in actual dollars can help you plan your budget. But not everyone will see the same amount added to their checks. 
According to Social Security's October 14 announcement, nearly 72 million beneficiaries will receive the increase, while Supplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients will see higher payments beginning December 31, 2026. The percentage adjustment is the same, but the dollar amounts differ depending on the benefit and household situation. 
Here's how six beneficiary groups compare, using SSA's official estimates for January 2027.

 Retired workers: $2,170 per month
Retired workers will see their estimated average monthly benefit rise from $2,095 to $2,170. That's an increase of $75 per month, or approximately $900 over a full year. 
However, $75 isn't a universal increase. Someone receiving $1,500 monthly would see roughly $54 more at 3.6%, while someone receiving $3,000 would gain about $108 before any deductions. Your actual benefit depends on factors such as your earnings history and when you started collecting Social Security.

 Retired couples: $3,355 per month
For retired couples in which both spouses receive benefits, SSA estimates the average combined monthly payment will rise from $3,238 to $3,355. That's an additional $117 per month, or approximately $1,404 annually. 
The distinction here is that $3,355 represents the couple's combined benefits, not a payment to each spouse. Individual benefits can differ substantially depending on each person's work history and claiming age, so couples should look at their separate benefit amounts when updating their household budgets. 
 Widowed mothers with two children: $4,074 per month
Families receiving survivor benefits can see a larger combined dollar increase because multiple eligible family members may collect payments. SSA projects the average benefit for a widowed mother with two children will rise from $3,932 to $4,074 per month. That's a $142 monthly increase, or about $1,704 annually. 
These benefits can help replace income after a worker dies — surviving spouses caring for qualifying children may receive benefits regardless of their own age, while eligible children can also receive payments.

 Widows and widowers living alone: $2,005 per month
For aged widows and widowers living alone, the estimated average monthly payment will increase from $1,936 to $2,005. That's $69 more each month, or approximately $828 over a full year. 
Survivor benefits generally depend on the deceased worker's earnings record and the surviving spouse's claiming age. Eligible spouses may receive up to 100% of the applicable survivor benefit when they reach the full retirement age for survivor benefits, which is between 66 and 67. 
 Disabled workers: $1,701 per month
Workers receiving Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) will see their estimated average monthly benefit rise from $1,642 to $1,701. That's an additional $59 per month, or roughly $708 annually. 
SSDI provides benefits to eligible workers whose qualifying disabilities prevent substantial work activity, based on their Social Security-covered earnings histories. Unlike SSI, which is needs-based, SSDI benefits generally depend on the worker's earnings record. 
 Disabled workers with spouses and children: $3,077 per month
Some families receive Social Security benefits based on a disabled worker's earnings record. For disabled workers with a spouse and one or more children receiving benefits, SSA estimates the average combined monthly payment will rise from $2,970 to $3,077. That's an increase of $107 per month, or approximately $1,284 annually. 
However, not every disabled worker's family qualifies for additional benefits. Eligibility depends on factors including age, marital status, and whether children meet the program's requirements.

 Bottom line
How much will the 2027 Social Security COLA actually add to your monthly income? The official 3.6% increase applies broadly, but the dollar impact depends on your existing benefit and whether other family members receive payments on the same earnings record. These six SSA averages offer useful benchmarks, not guarantees of what any particular household will collect. 
For your exact amount, check your my Social Security account or review the personalized notices mailed by the Social Security Administration. Remember that Medicare premiums and other deductions can affect what reaches your bank account. Knowing your actual payment before January can help you eliminate some stress living on Social Security and adjust your household budget accordingly.
